svg.aria-label: How to write ૂ — ટ — ઈ — ઢ: 4 parts, ૂ, ટ, ઈ, ઢ, one after another
svg.title: Writing ૂ — ટ — ઈ — ઢ
svg.desc: 4 parts written one after another: ૂ, ટ, ઈ, ઢ (gujarati). The parts are in the order the hand writes them, which in Gujarati is the order they are typed: each sign comes after its consonant, even the i sign, which sits to the left of it. Each sign is drawn on its own, without the consonant it attaches to. Each part has its own group of frames; frame N of a group shows movements 1 to N of that part, the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished part, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansGujarati-Static.ttf. Each part is drawn at its own scale from its own cited stroke order, so the strip does not show how large the parts are next to each other, how far apart they sit, or any join between them. Stroke order: ૂ: Tejas Gajjar, KanoAI, Gujarati barakhadi centre-line stroke templates (interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi), commit 9d3e294, 1_k/5_koo.svg, group g1 (stroke g1s0): the uu sign drawn after the consonant (GitHub, 2026) <https://github.com/gajjartejas/KanoAI/tree/9d3e2949a3f265448e430e15329093ea3aa516b8/interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi>; ટ: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, ટ animation, first SVG path <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>; ઈ: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, ઈ animation, first SVG path <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>; ઢ: t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, ઢ animation, first SVG path <https://www.t30apps.com/gujarati-alphabet-writing/>. Source notes on variation: ૂ: In the template for કૂ, and in all 32 consonant rows whose consonant keeps its bare outline, ૂ is one pen-down run that starts low in the middle, curls left and up to the top, then sweeps right and down, ending at the lower right. HP Labs India's Lipi Toolkit Devanagari recognizer (native writers' pen traces of the matching Devanagari sign, written alone) agrees: all 83 of its stored prototypes of the uu sign are one stroke; 96% end on the right and 93% move downward overall. KanoAI's templates are hand-made centre lines, one path per pen-down run, which the app animates in the author's handwriting order and direction; one template per sign is placed beside every consonant, so the row counts show consistency, not separate writers. KanoAI's LICENSE file says MIT while its README says GNU GPL, so the licence is ambiguous: only facts are cited here (order, start, direction and pen lifts), and no template path data was copied. The path is fitted to the bundled Noto Sans Gujarati outline of the sign on its own. Handwriting varies by writer. ટ: The teaching app animates ટ as one continuous pen-down run in its first SVG path; its remaining path slots are empty. The run begins at the upper left, sweeps right across the rounded upper turn, bends diagonally down-left through the middle, then circles clockwise around the broad lower bowl and finishes on its right side without lifting. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the upper turn, diagonal middle transition, and broad lower bowl, but its printed turns are broader and more angular than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's upper-turn-to-middle-to-lower-bowl order and zero-lift evidence while fitting the continuous run to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, or slant the turns, transition, bowl, and terminals differently. ઈ: The teaching app animates ઈ as one continuous pen-down run in its first SVG path; its remaining path slots are empty. The run begins at the upper-left, sweeps left and down through the small upper loop, returns through the narrow middle crossing, circles the broad lower body, then rises along the right side and curls clockwise around the extended top hook without lifting. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the small upper-left loop, narrow middle crossing, broad lower loop, and extended top curl, but its printed lower body is wider and its high curl more rounded than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's upper-loop-to-lower-loop-to-extended-curl order and zero-lift evidence while fitting the motion to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, or slant the loops and curl differently. ઢ: The teaching app animates ઢ as one continuous pen-down run in its first SVG path; its remaining path slots are empty. The run begins at the upper left, sweeps right across the high shoulder, descends through the middle into the left side of the broad outer lower bowl, circles around its base and right side, then continues directly around the small inner loop without lifting. The app explicitly says that depicted forms and stroke orders can differ by source and should be treated as one variant, not a universal standard. The bundled Noto Sans Gujarati glyph preserves the high shoulder, broad outer bowl, and inner loop, but its printed shoulder is tighter and its bowl and counter more angular than the animated school-hand form. This learner path preserves the source's shoulder-to-outer-bowl-to-inner-loop order and zero-lift evidence while fitting the continuous run to the font's ink. Individual handwriting may narrow, round, simplify, retrace, or slant the shoulder, bowl, counter, loop, and terminal differently.
svg.text: How it is written — 4 parts, one after another
Part 1 of 4 — one unbroken stroke · 3 movements
Part 3 of 4 — one unbroken stroke · 4 movements
Part 1: stroke order after Tejas Gajjar, KanoAI, Gujarati barakhadi centre-line stroke templates (interpolate-svg/svgs/barakhadi), commit 9d3e294,
1_k/5_koo.svg, group g1 (stroke g1s0): the uu sign drawn after the consonant (GitHub, 2026)
Part 2: stroke order after t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, ટ animation, first SVG path
Part 3: stroke order after t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, ઈ animation, first SVG path
Part 4: stroke order after t30apps.com, ‘Gujarati Alphabet Writing Practice’, version 1.0, ઢ animation, first SVG path
This order is attested, not standardised; the source records where it varies.
